what: Healthpeak owns laboratory buildings leased to biotech companies, medical offices next to hospitals, and some senior housing. It is a landlord to health care rather than a provider of it.
customers: Biotech and pharmaceutical tenants in Boston, San Francisco and San Diego, and physician groups in medical offices.
money: research buildings leased to life science companies
medical office buildings, mostly near hospitals
moat: Laboratory buildings cannot be converted from ordinary offices: ventilation, floor loading and power are purpose-built, and they cluster in a few cities where the scientists are.
risks: Biotech funding fell and lab vacancy has risen in every major cluster
A lot of new lab space was built in 2021 and 2022 and is still being absorbed
opportunities: $610M of free cash flow and analysts see about 17% upside
Medical office buildings next to hospitals stay full regardless of the biotech cycle
Revenue grew from $1.9B to $2.8B in four years, helped by the Physicians Realty merger
watch: Lab leasing activity and the occupancy trend in the biggest clusters.
